pr.title: feat: PR Triage Bot — Phase 1 MVP with layered AI review
pr.author: jgodwin-ai

executiveSummary: This PR introduces a complete full-stack PR Triage Bot MVP: a multi-stage LLM analysis pipeline (Anthropic SDK + Claude CLI), an Express REST/WebSocket backend with async job model, and a React frontend with real-time progress and annotated diff views. Reviewers should concentrate on the backend-llm-pipeline (core agent orchestration and provider abstractions), backend-api (async job lifecycle, in-memory result store, WebSocket broadcast), and backend-github-service (auth, pagination edge cases) — these three clusters contain all meaningful business logic risk. The 50-file coverage-artifacts cluster is auto-generated and should be gitignored; documentation and config clusters can be skimmed.

clusters.name: Backend LLM Agent Pipeline
clusters.summary: The core multi-stage analysis pipeline that orchestrates per-file LLM analysis, clustering, and ranking/synthesis. Includes the LLM client abstraction, both provider implementations (Anthropic SDK and Claude CLI), and all three agent modules. This is the highest-risk cluster as it contains the primary business logic.

files.summary: Introduces a new orchestration pipeline that coordinates three sequential stages (per-file analysis, clustering, and ranking/synthesis) with concurrency limiting and real-time WebSocket progress messages. This is a core logic module that drives the entire PR analysis workflow.

annotations.message: The concurrency limit of 5 is hardcoded. Consider making it a configurable parameter or environment variable so it can be tuned for different deployment environments.

The `completed` counter is mutated by concurrent closures without synchronization. In Node.js this is safe due to the single-threaded event loop, but the progress messages may arrive out of order since multiple limits can resolve in the same microtask batch.

The catch block re-throws the error after sending a WebSocket error message, which is correct. Callers should be aware that the promise will reject so they can handle cleanup (e.g., closing the WebSocket connection).
The empty-files early-return path correctly emits a 'complete' message and returns a well-formed PRAnalysis, ensuring consumers always receive a terminal message regardless of input.

files.summary: Introduces a new file analyzer agent that builds LLM prompts for per-file diff analysis and parses the structured JSON response into a FileAnalysis object. This is a core piece of the automated PR triage pipeline, enabling per-file categorization, impact scoring, and inline annotations.

annotations.message: The result of extractJSON is cast to `any`, bypassing TypeScript type safety. If the LLM returns unexpected or missing fields, runtime errors may silently produce malformed FileAnalysis objects. Consider adding validation (e.g., zod schema) before mapping fields.

The `file` parameter type is inline and uses `patch: string`, but files without diffs (lockfiles, binaries) may have an undefined or empty patch. Consider using `patch?: string` and handling the missing-patch case gracefully to match how callers already handle such files.
annotations defaults to an empty array when absent from the parsed response, which is a safe fallback. This is consistent with the schema where annotations are optional.

files.summary: Introduces a new clustering agent module that groups analyzed PR files into logical change clusters using an LLM. This is a key piece of the PR triage pipeline, enabling structured review organization by delegating cluster logic to the LLM and mapping results back to typed FileAnalysis objects.
files.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,63 @@
+import type { LLMClient } from "../llm-client.js";
+import type { FileAnalysis, ChangeCluster } from "../../types.js";
+import { extractJSON } from "./extract-json.js";
+
+export function buildClusteringPrompt(files: FileAnalysis[]): string {
+  const fileSummaries = files
+    .map(
+      (f) =>
+        `- ${f.path} [${f.category}, impact=${f.impactScore}]: ${f.summary}`
+    )
+    .join("\n");
+
+  return `Group these PR file changes into logical clusters of related changes.
+
+Files analyzed:
+${fileSummaries}
+
+Respond with JSON only — no markdown fences, no commentary. Use this exact schema:
+{
+  "clusters": [
+    {
+      "id": "short-kebab-id",
+      "name": "Human readable cluster name",
+      "summary": "2-3 sentences explaining what this group of changes does together",
+      "tag": "needs-review" | "low-risk" | "boilerplate" | "style-only",
+      "priority": <number, 1=highest priority for reviewer>,
+      "filePaths": ["path/to/file1.ts", "path/to/file2.ts"]
+    }
+  ]
+}
+
+Clustering guidelines:
+- Group files that work together to accomplish one logical change
+- A file should appear in exactly one cluster
+- Tag clusters based on the highest-impact file in the group
+- "needs-review" = contains logic changes that could introduce bugs
+- "low-risk" = config, docs, or simple changes unlikely to break anything
+- "boilerplate" = generated or repetitive code
+- "style-only" = formatting, naming, no behavior change
+- Priority 1 = most important for reviewer, higher numbers = less important`;
+}
+
+export async function clusterFiles(
+  files: FileAnalysis[],
+  client: LLMClient
+): Promise<ChangeCluster[]> {
+  const text = await client.complete(buildClusteringPrompt(files));
+  const parsed = extractJSON(text) as any;
+
+  const filesByPath = new Map(files.map((f) => [f.path, f]));
+
+  return parsed.clusters.map(
+    (c: { id: string; name: string; summary: string; tag: string; priority: number; filePaths: string[] }) => ({
+      id: c.id,
+      name: c.name,
+      summary: c.summary,
+      tag: c.tag as ChangeCluster["tag"],
+      priority: c.priority,
+      files: c.filePaths.map((p: string) => filesByPath.get(p)).filter(Boolean) as FileAnalysis[],
+      insights: [],
+    })
+  );
+}

annotations.message: The LLM response is cast with 'as any' and then accessed without validation. If the LLM returns malformed JSON or a missing 'clusters' field, this will throw a runtime error with no helpful message. Consider adding a schema check or try/catch with a descriptive error.

Files not found in the filesByPath map are silently filtered out via .filter(Boolean). A file path in the LLM response that doesn't match any analyzed file will be dropped without any warning, making it hard to debug mismatches.

The tag field is cast with 'as ChangeCluster["tag"]' without validation. If the LLM returns an unexpected tag value, it will be accepted silently. Consider validating against the allowed tag literals before casting.

The prompt instructs the LLM to respond with JSON only and no markdown fences, but LLM responses can vary. The extractJSON utility presumably handles stripping fences — confirm it handles edge cases like partial markdown or leading/trailing whitespace robustly.

files.summary: Introduces a new ranking agent that uses an LLM to produce an executive summary, re-rank change clusters by review priority, and estimate time saved. This is a critical piece of the PR triage pipeline as it synthesizes upstream cluster analysis into actionable reviewer guidance.

annotations.message: The parsed LLM response is cast as `any` without schema validation. If the LLM returns unexpected fields or omits required ones, downstream code will silently use undefined values. Consider adding runtime validation (e.g. Zod) or at least null-checks for executiveSummary, timeSaved, and clusterUpdates.

Clusters not returned by the LLM (i.e. present in clusterMap but absent from parsed.clusterUpdates) are silently dropped from the result. If the LLM omits a cluster, the caller loses it entirely. Consider falling back to the original cluster entry for any ID not returned.

Unknown cluster IDs from the LLM are warned and skipped, which is good defensive behavior, but the warning goes only to console. In a production service, consider surfacing this as a structured error or metric so silent data loss can be detected.

Sorting happens after the loop; clusters with duplicate priority values will have non-deterministic relative order. If stable ordering matters, consider a secondary sort key (e.g. original index or cluster id) to keep output deterministic across runs.

There is no retry or error-handling around the LLM call or JSON extraction. A malformed LLM response will propagate an unhandled exception to the caller. Consider wrapping with try/catch and deciding on a fallback strategy (e.g. return clusters unsorted with a placeholder summary).

files.summary: Introduces a utility function that parses JSON from LLM responses by stripping optional markdown fences before attempting JSON.parse, throwing a descriptive error on failure. This centralizes a common LLM output-handling pattern and improves reliability when Claude or other models wrap JSON in code blocks.

annotations.message: The regex requires the content to be surrounded by triple backticks but does not handle cases where there are multiple fenced blocks in the response; only the first match is used, which may silently discard additional JSON blocks.
Truncating the raw text to 200 characters in the error message is helpful for brevity, but consider logging the full text at a debug level so parsing failures are easier to diagnose in production.

The return type is 'unknown', which is correct for safety, but callers will need to cast or validate the result. Consider pairing this function with a generic overload that accepts a Zod schema or type guard to return a typed value.

files.summary: Introduces a new LLMClient interface and LLMProvider type to abstract away the concrete LLM implementation, allowing agents to depend on a common interface rather than a specific provider. This is foundational scaffolding that enables provider swapping without changing agent code.
files.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,13 @@
+/**
+ * LLM Client abstraction — swap between Claude CLI, Anthropic SDK, or any other provider.
+ *
+ * All agents depend on this interface, not a concrete implementation.
+ * To switch providers, change the factory function in index.ts.
+ */
+
+export interface LLMClient {
+  /** Send a prompt and get a text response back. */
+  complete(prompt: string): Promise<string>;
+}
+
+export type LLMProvider = "claude-cli" | "anthropic-sdk";

annotations.message: The interface only exposes a single `complete` method. If streaming, token counting, or structured output are needed later, the interface will need to be extended or a separate interface introduced.

LLMProvider is defined here but the factory function it references (in index.ts) is not yet visible in this diff. Ensure the factory enforces exhaustive handling of all LLMProvider values to avoid silent fallbacks when new providers are added.

files.summary: Adds a new LLM client implementation that uses the Anthropic SDK directly with API key authentication, implementing the LLMClient interface. This provides an alternative to any IAM/OAuth-based client and is explicitly kept as a fallback option for API key auth.

annotations.message: The comment explicitly marks this as a 'keep around' fallback — consider adding a TODO or tracking issue so it doesn't become dead code inadvertently.

The apiKey is stored only in the Anthropic client instance; if callers pass an empty string or undefined cast to string, the SDK will silently use an invalid key. Consider validating that apiKey is non-empty in the constructor.

The complete() method handles only the first content block and throws on non-text blocks; if the model ever returns tool_use or other block types first this will surface as a runtime error rather than a graceful degradation.

files.summary: Introduces a new LLM client implementation that delegates to the `claude` CLI via child process, allowing the service to leverage existing Claude Code authentication without requiring a separate API key. This is a significant addition that enables a zero-config path for running LLM completions in development or authenticated environments.

annotations.message: Using execFileAsync with user-supplied prompt strings passed directly as CLI arguments. If `prompt` ever contains untrusted content, this could be exploited; ensure callers sanitize or bound the input before passing it here.
The 2-minute timeout may be too short for very large diffs or slow model responses; consider making this configurable via constructor opts alongside model and maxTokens.

The default model is set to the shorthand 'sonnet' rather than a fully-qualified model ID (e.g. 'claude-sonnet-4-5'). If the CLI resolves this alias to different versions over time, behavior could change silently — consider pinning to a specific model ID.
stderr from the CLI process is silently discarded. Capturing and logging stderr would help diagnose failures such as auth errors, rate limits, or model unavailability.

clusters.name: Backend API Server and Routes
clusters.summary: The Express server entry point, REST route handlers for analysis and config status, WebSocket broadcast module, and shared backend type definitions. Together these define the full API surface that the frontend depends on, including the async job model, in-memory result store, and real-time progress messaging.

files.summary: Introduces the Express server entry point, wiring together REST routes, WebSocket broadcasting, and the multi-stage PR analysis pipeline. This is a foundational file that defines application startup, LLM client selection, and static-file serving for production.

annotations.message: Both '/api/analyze' and '/api/analysis' are mounted to the same analyzeRouter, which means any route defined in that router will be reachable under two different paths. This is likely unintentional and can cause confusion or duplicate side effects (e.g., two analysis runs triggered by clients hitting different URLs).

createLLMClient silently falls back to ClaudeCliClient when no API key is provided. In a production environment this fallback may be unexpected; consider logging a warning or making the fallback explicit in documentation.

Error handling in startPipeline broadcasts the error and stores an error state, but does not distinguish between transient errors (network timeouts) and permanent failures. Adding error classification or a retry hint in the broadcast payload would improve client-side UX.

The wildcard 'GET *' catch-all route checks req.path.startsWith('/api/') to return a 404, but API routes are already registered before this handler, so this guard is only meaningful for paths that somehow fall through. A more defensive approach would be to register a dedicated 404 handler specifically for /api/* after all API routers.
The server is exported alongside app, which is useful for testing. Ensure test teardown calls server.close() to avoid open handle warnings, especially given the conditional PORT=0 logic for VITEST.

files.summary: Introduces the core /analyze Express router that accepts PR URLs, validates inputs, spawns async analysis pipelines via a delegate function, and stores results in an in-memory Map with a 100-entry cap. This is the primary API surface for triggering and polling PR analysis jobs.

annotations.message: In-memory store with a naive FIFO pruning strategy is not safe for concurrent deployments or process restarts — all in-flight or completed analyses will be lost on restart, and pruning removes the oldest entries regardless of whether callers are still polling them.

pruneAnalyses deletes the first N keys in insertion order but Map iteration order can be surprising under concurrent inserts; consider a proper LRU or TTL-based eviction so recently-started analyses are not discarded while still running.
effectiveGithubToken check correctly falls back to the environment variable, providing a sensible deployment default without requiring every request to supply a token.
The trailing '|| undefined' is redundant — if both anthropicApiKey and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY are falsy, the expression already evaluates to undefined; remove for clarity.

If startPipeline is not registered on app.locals the analysis is stored as 'running' but will never transition to a completed or error state, leaving callers polling indefinitely with no timeout or error feedback.
pruneAnalyses is called before validation, so a burst of invalid requests will still consume the eviction budget and potentially evict valid analyses.

files.summary: Adds a new /status endpoint that exposes whether the GitHub token and Anthropic API key are configured, along with which LLM provider will be used. This is useful for health checks and client-side conditional UI, but exposes configuration state publicly.

annotations.message: The /status endpoint is unauthenticated and reveals server configuration details (which API keys are present, which LLM provider is active). If this backend is publicly accessible, this leaks operational metadata. Consider adding authentication or restricting to internal/admin routes.

The llmProvider field exposes the fallback strategy (claude-cli vs anthropic-sdk). This is useful for debugging but couples clients to internal implementation details; if the provider logic changes, clients relying on this field may need updates.

files.summary: Introduces a new WebSocket module that sets up a WebSocket server and provides a broadcast utility for pushing typed messages to all connected clients. This establishes the real-time communication layer for the backend, enabling server-initiated pushes to the frontend.

annotations.message: Error handler is attached on each connection but only logs the message; consider whether any cleanup or reconnection logic is needed on error.
broadcast serializes the message once and fans out, which is correct. Consider adding a try/catch around client.send to avoid one failing client aborting the loop for the rest.
The 'connection' handler only wires up an error listener; if per-connection message handling (e.g., pings, authentication) is needed later, this is where it should be added.

files.summary: Introduces the full TypeScript type system for the PR analysis application, defining core interfaces for PR metadata, file-level analysis, clustering, diff annotations, WebSocket messaging, and analysis requests. This is a foundational addition that establishes the data contract shared across the backend.

annotations.message: PRAnalysis.id is untyped as string — consider using a branded type or UUID type alias to prevent accidental assignment of arbitrary strings.
ChangeCluster.tag uses a narrow union of four literals; if new tag values are added later, this type will need to be updated in all consumers simultaneously.
FileAnalysis.category mirrors the analysis prompt's category guide — keeping these in sync with the prompt is a maintenance concern as the guide evolves.
FileAnalysis.diff stores the raw diff string inline, which could be very large for files with many changes and inflate memory usage when many FileAnalysis objects are held in memory simultaneously.

anthropicApiKey and githubToken are optional strings passed in the request body — ensure these are never logged or persisted, and consider documenting that they are ephemeral credentials expected to be short-lived.

clusters.name: Backend GitHub Service
clusters.summary: Encapsulates all GitHub API interactions: PR URL parsing, Octokit client construction, and paginated file/metadata fetching. This is a critical integration boundary where auth tokens, rate limits, and pagination edge cases can cause silent data loss.

files.summary: Introduces a new GitHub service module that encapsulates PR URL parsing, Octokit client creation, and paginated PR data fetching (metadata + files). This is a foundational service layer that centralizes GitHub API interactions for the rest of the backend.

annotations.message: The manual pagination loop only includes files that have a 'patch' field, silently dropping binary files, renamed files, and other patch-less entries. This means 'allFiles' may have fewer entries than 'metadata.fileCount', which could confuse consumers expecting a 1:1 correspondence. Consider including all files (with an empty/null patch) to preserve accurate counts.

The loop termination condition 'filesResponse.data.length < 100' is fragile — if the API returns exactly 100 items on the last page, an extra empty request is made. Using 'octokit.paginate' instead of a manual loop is more idiomatic and avoids this off-by-one edge case.

The 'patch' field in the PRData files array is typed as 'string', but the GitHub API returns it as 'string | undefined'. Typing it as 'string | undefined' (or filtering explicitly) makes the interface more accurately reflect the data shape.

'createOctokit' is a thin wrapper around the Octokit constructor. It is useful for dependency injection and testability, but callers should be aware that the token is passed in plaintext — ensure it is sourced from environment variables and never logged.

clusters.name: Backend Test Suite
clusters.summary: Integration and unit tests for all backend modules: route handlers (analyze, config, health), service agents (file-analyzer, clustering, ranking, extract-json), GitHub service, pipeline orchestration, and WebSocket broadcast. These tests collectively validate the full analysis workflow and provide the coverage data committed alongside this PR.

files.summary: Adds a comprehensive integration test suite for the /api/analyze and /api/analysis/:id endpoints, covering input validation, API key handling (env vars vs request body), and status polling via a seeded in-memory store. This directly validates the core analysis pipeline entry points and their error boundaries.

annotations.message: Setting process.env directly in a test without cleanup (no afterEach or try/finally) risks leaking env state if the assertion throws before the cleanup lines at the end of other tests. Consider using beforeEach/afterEach hooks or a helper to snapshot and restore env.

The manual save/restore pattern for environment variables is repeated across multiple tests. Extracting a withEnv() helper or using beforeEach/afterEach would reduce boilerplate and make cleanup more reliable if a test assertion fails mid-flight.

The test asserts that a missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY still returns 202, documenting that the key is optional. This is worth a comment in the test body so future maintainers understand the intentional design decision rather than assuming it is an oversight.

setAnalysis is imported from the production module to seed test state, which tightly couples tests to an internal helper. If the in-memory store is later replaced with a different backing (Redis, DB), these tests will need updates. A test-only seeding interface or dependency injection would be more resilient.

The failed-analysis test expects HTTP 200 even for error status. Consider whether a 4xx or 5xx response would be more appropriate for a failed analysis, or add a comment explaining why 200 is the intended behaviour for this case.

files.summary: Adds a new test suite for the GET /api/config/status endpoint, verifying that the response correctly reflects whether ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and GITHUB_TOKEN environment variables are set and reports the appropriate llmProvider. These tests ensure the configuration status route behaves correctly under both configured and unconfigured states.

annotations.message: Mutating process.env directly in tests can cause race conditions or state leakage if tests run concurrently. Consider using a library like 'jest-environment-variables' or mocking the env at the module level for safer isolation.
The test assumes the llmProvider value is exactly 'anthropic-sdk' when keys are present. If the provider resolution logic changes, this test will catch regressions, which is good.
Consider adding a test case where only one of the two keys is set to verify partial configuration is handled correctly and the llmProvider fallback behaves as expected.
The top-level afterAll closes the server, which is correct for cleanup. Ensure the server import from index.js is the same instance used by supertest to avoid port conflicts in CI.

files.summary: Adds a new integration test for the GET /api/health endpoint, verifying it returns a 200 status and a { status: 'ok' } body. This ensures the health check route is functioning correctly and provides a safety net for regressions.

annotations.message: Imports both `app` and `server` from the main index — ensure index.ts exports these named exports; if not, this will cause a runtime import error.
afterAll closes the server to prevent open handles after the test suite, which is good practice for vitest/supertest teardown.
Consider adding a test for an unexpected HTTP method (e.g., POST) to verify the route only accepts GET requests, improving coverage of the health endpoint contract.

files.summary: Adds a new test suite covering the `clusterFiles` and `buildClusteringPrompt` functions in the clustering agent service, verifying correct LLM response parsing, file path resolution, empty result handling, and error throwing on invalid JSON. These tests are important for validating the core clustering logic that groups PR files into review clusters.

annotations.message: The test verifies that filePaths not matching any input file are silently dropped. Consider also asserting that no error or warning is thrown/logged when unknown paths are encountered, to make the expected behavior fully explicit.

The error message assertion uses a string literal 'Failed to parse LLM response as JSON'. If this message ever changes in the implementation, the test will fail silently during refactors — consider importing or exporting the error message as a constant to keep the test and source in sync.
There is no test for malformed but valid JSON (e.g., a response that parses but lacks a `clusters` key). Adding a test for this edge case would improve resilience coverage of the parsing logic.

files.summary: Adds a new test suite for the extractJSON utility function, covering plain JSON parsing, markdown-fenced JSON (with and without language tags), whitespace trimming, and error handling including message truncation at 200 characters. These tests ensure the LLM response parser behaves correctly across common edge cases.

annotations.message: The truncation test uses a try/catch without a fail assertion — if extractJSON unexpectedly succeeds or throws a different error, the test will silently pass. Consider adding an explicit expect.assertions(2) or a fail() call to ensure the catch block is actually exercised.

The invalid-JSON error test calls extractJSON twice with the same input. Consider extracting the input into a variable and combining assertions, or using a single toThrow matcher that checks both conditions, to avoid redundant execution.

Test file imports from '../../../src/services/agents/extract-json.js' using a .js extension — confirm the TypeScript/Vitest config is set up to resolve .js imports to .ts sources, otherwise this path may fail at runtime.

files.summary: Adds a new test suite for the file-analyzer service, covering prompt building, successful LLM response parsing, markdown-wrapped JSON handling, and invalid JSON error handling. These tests validate the core contract of the analyzeFile function and improve confidence in the LLM integration layer.

annotations.message: The markdown-wrapped JSON test only checks path and category — consider also asserting summary, impactScore, and diff to match the coverage level of the first test case.

Consider adding a test for malformed-but-valid JSON that doesn't match the expected schema (e.g., missing required fields like 'category'), to ensure schema validation errors are also handled gracefully.

files.summary: Adds a new test suite for the rankAndSynthesize and buildRankingPrompt functions, covering prompt construction, cluster re-ranking, unknown ID handling, invalid JSON error propagation, and priority sorting. These tests establish behavioral contracts for the ranking agent and will catch regressions in LLM response parsing and cluster update logic.

annotations.message: The 'skips unknown cluster IDs' test expects result.clusters to have length 1 (only 'auth'), but the 'docs' cluster from sampleClusters is also not in clusterUpdates — this implicitly verifies that clusters not mentioned in clusterUpdates are dropped, not just unknown IDs. The test name and warning assertion focus on 'unknown-cluster', but the broader behavior (missing clusters are also dropped) is exercised without being explicitly documented.

The 'returns fewer clusters when LLMClient returns fewer clusterUpdates' test overlaps significantly with the 'skips unknown cluster IDs' case. Consider clarifying the distinction: this test verifies intentional omission (no unknown ID warning expected), whereas the previous test verifies graceful handling of truly unknown IDs. Adding a negative assertion (e.g., expect(console.warn).not.toHaveBeenCalled()) would make the distinction explicit.

The invalid JSON test asserts rejects.toThrow('Failed to parse LLM response as JSON'), which ties the test to a specific error message string. If the error message ever changes, this test will fail even if the behavior is correct. Consider matching on error type or a more stable substring.

Both sample clusters have empty 'files' and 'insights' arrays. Adding at least one entry in one cluster would provide better coverage for any logic in buildRankingPrompt or rankAndSynthesize that iterates over these fields.

files.summary: Adds a comprehensive test suite for the GitHub service covering URL parsing and PR data fetching, including edge cases like null users, binary file filtering, and pagination beyond 100 files. These tests directly validate critical service behavior that underpins the PR triage bot's core functionality.

annotations.message: The pagination test mocks listFiles with mockResolvedValueOnce twice but the implementation likely uses octokit.paginate (per recent commits) rather than manual page-by-page calls. This test may not accurately reflect actual pagination behavior and could pass even if the real paginate logic is broken.

Binary file filtering test (patch undefined) is valuable but only covers the 'added' status case. Consider also testing 'modified' status files without a patch to ensure filtering is based on patch presence, not file status.
The first fetchPR test only asserts files[0] but not files[1]. Adding an assertion for files[1] (README.md) would improve coverage and catch any ordering issues.
The mockOctokit is typed as 'any' throughout — consider defining a minimal typed interface or using vi.mocked to improve type safety and catch shape mismatches at compile time.

files.summary: Adds a comprehensive test suite for the runPipeline service covering happy path execution, empty PR early return, and error propagation from each of the three pipeline stages. These tests verify both the return value shape and the WebSocket message emissions, ensuring pipeline observability is correctly implemented.

annotations.message: Using 'any' type for messages array and onMessage callback reduces type safety; consider typing these as WSMessage[] using the actual message type from types.ts for better compile-time guarantees.

The empty-PR test asserts exactly 1 message of type 'complete'; if the implementation emits a status message before the early return check, this assertion will fail — worth confirming the pipeline implementation emits no status messages before the empty-files guard.

Accessing errorMsg.error without first asserting errorMsg is defined (toBeDefined check is present but on the previous line) is safe in practice, but if the assertion fails the subsequent property access will throw a confusing secondary error rather than a clear test failure message.

analyzeFile is expected to be called twice (once per file), but mockFileAnalysis only contains data for src/a.ts; the second call for src/b.ts will also resolve to the same mockFileAnalysis, which may mask bugs in per-file path handling downstream.

files.summary: Adds a comprehensive test suite for the WebSocket server module, covering connection acceptance, multi-client broadcast, empty-client broadcast resilience, and skipping non-OPEN clients. These tests validate the core real-time communication layer used for streaming analysis progress to the frontend.

annotations.message: The outer `server` variable is shared across tests but only one test uses it; the other tests create their own local servers. This is fine but slightly inconsistent — consider making all servers local for symmetry.

afterAll only closes `server` (used by the first test). Servers created in other `it` blocks (server2, server3, server4) are closed inline, but if those tests throw before reaching server.close(), the servers may leak. Consider wrapping per-test servers in try/finally or afterEach hooks.

Waiting for both clients to open before broadcasting is the correct approach, but there is a small race: the broadcast fires immediately after both 'open' events resolve, with no guarantee the server has registered both sockets internally. In practice the wss 'connection' event fires before the client 'open' event, so this is safe — worth noting as a subtle ordering assumption.

Waiting for the 'close' event on the client socket is good, but the server-side wss4 still has the socket in its clients set during the CLOSING state. If the broadcast fires before the server processes the TCP close, the socket's readyState may still be CLOSING (not CLOSED). The test is designed to verify no-throw in that scenario — consider adding a brief assertion or comment clarifying the expected readyState value at the point of broadcast.

annotations.message: The assertion 'expect(allInstances.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)' is weak — it will pass even if only one instance exists when more specific counts are expected. Consider asserting an exact count (e.g., toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2)) to better validate that both the breadcrumb and the cluster detail heading render the name.

The test imports from '../../src/components/AnalysisView.js' using a .js extension — this is typical for ESM/Vite setups but can be fragile if the project migrates. Confirm that the test configuration resolves .js imports to .tsx source files as expected.

The 'makeAnalysis' helper is imported from '../helpers.js' — ensure this helper produces data that represents the full expected structure (executive summary, at least two clusters with names 'Core Logic Changes' and 'Style Updates') so tests don't silently pass against stub data.

files.summary: Adds a new test suite for the Breadcrumbs component covering rendering, accessibility attributes, and click interaction. This matters because it validates both functional behavior (separator rendering, button roles, onClick callbacks) and accessibility compliance (aria-current and aria-label on nav).

annotations.message: Test relies on container.textContent containing '/' to verify separators; this is a loose assertion. Consider querying separator elements directly to make the test more precise and resilient to implementation changes.

The aria-current='page' test queries by text then checks the attribute on the returned element. If the component wraps the text in a child node, getAttribute may return null. Consider using a more targeted selector or role query to ensure the attribute check is reliable.
JSX is used without an explicit React import; ensure the tsconfig/vite config has jsx set to 'react-jsx' (automatic runtime) so the transform is picked up correctly in the test environment.

files.summary: Adds a new test file for the ClusterDetail component covering rendering of cluster name/summary, per-file DiffView rendering, and display of file count and priority. These tests establish baseline coverage for a key UI component in the PR triage frontend.

annotations.message: Imports use .js extensions for local modules (helpers.js, ClusterDetail.js), which is correct for ESM resolution but worth confirming the test runner and tsconfig are aligned to avoid resolution errors.

Using toBeTruthy() for text presence checks is loose; prefer getByText(...) to throw on absence (which it already does) and drop the toBeTruthy() assertion, or use toBeInTheDocument() from @testing-library/jest-dom for more idiomatic assertions.
The regex /priority 2/ is tightly coupled to the rendered text format. Consider defining a constant or using a more robust query (e.g., getByTestId) so the test doesn't break on minor copy changes.

There is no test for interactive behavior (e.g., expand/collapse of the collapsible files accordion introduced in recent commits). Consider adding a test for that interaction to ensure the feature is covered.

files.summary: Adds a new test file for the ClusterList component covering rendering, tag badge styling, click/keyboard interaction, and accessibility attributes. This ensures the component correctly handles user interaction and meets basic a11y requirements.

annotations.message: Checking className directly on the element assumes the tag text node is the element with the CSS class. If the tag text is in a child element this may pass correctly, but if the structure changes this test could produce false positives or break unexpectedly.

The Enter key test retrieves items via getAllByRole('button') which depends on the render order matching the clusters array order. Consider using a more explicit query (e.g., by accessible name) to avoid fragile index-based selection.
Same index-based fragility as the Enter key test — using getAllByRole('button')[1] is positional. A name-based query would make this test more robust and readable.
Accessibility test verifying role='button' and tabIndex=0 is valuable. Consider also asserting that aria-label or accessible name is present on each item so screen reader users get meaningful labels.

annotations.message: The test queries all divs inside .diff-code and finds by textContent, which is fragile if the component wraps line text in nested elements. Consider querying by a more specific selector (e.g., a data-testid or a dedicated line class) to avoid brittle DOM traversal.

screen.getByText("src/index.ts") will throw (not just fail) if the element is absent, so the toBeTruthy assertion is redundant. This is consistent with Testing Library best practices where getBy* already asserts presence, but the extra expect calls add noise.

The test asserts that 'Annotations' heading is absent when the annotations array is empty, but it does not verify via makeFileAnalysis defaults that the default fixture actually populates annotations. If makeFileAnalysis defaults to a non-empty annotations array the test could silently pass for the wrong reason — confirm the default or make the empty-annotations intent explicit.

annotations.message: Checking className directly is brittle — consider using a CSS module or data-testid attribute to assert styling intent more robustly, since class names can change with build tooling.

The test imports use .js extensions (ExecutiveSummary.js, helpers.js) which is correct for ESM resolution, but ensure the test environment (vitest config) is set up to handle TypeScript source files with .js import aliases.
Consider adding a test for when timeSaved is undefined/null (not just empty string) to cover all falsy edge cases for conditional rendering.

files.summary: Adds a new test suite for the LandingPage component covering rendering, config fetching on mount, conditional display of GitHub token field, and loading state behavior. These tests improve confidence in the component's core user-facing interactions and integration with the useAnalysis hook.

annotations.message: The module mock wraps mockUseAnalysis so per-test overrides work; this pattern is correct but relies on the outer vi.fn() reference being stable across the module boundary.

The global fetch stub in beforeEach is overridden in several individual tests, which can lead to confusion. Consider removing the beforeEach stub and letting each test that needs fetch set its own, making dependencies explicit.

The test asserts queryByPlaceholderText('GitHub Token') is null after only waiting for 'Analyze PR' to appear. If the token field is removed asynchronously after the button renders, this assertion could pass prematurely; consider wrapping it in a waitFor or asserting after the same await.

Casting button as HTMLButtonElement to check .disabled is fine, but using expect(button).toBeDisabled() from @testing-library/jest-dom (if available) would be more idiomatic and produce clearer failure messages.

files.summary: Adds a new test file for the useAnalysis hook covering POST request behavior, error state handling for non-OK HTTP responses, network failures, and non-JSON error bodies. These tests provide important coverage for the hook's async fetch and error-handling logic.

annotations.message: MockWebSocket is defined but none of its event handlers (onopen, onmessage, onclose) are exercised in any test. If useAnalysis uses WebSocket for streaming analysis progress, tests covering WebSocket message handling and the onComplete callback would increase confidence.

startAnalysis is called with only one argument ('bad-url') which may not match the function signature that expects prUrl, anthropicApiKey, and githubToken. If missing required arguments cause a different code path (e.g., early validation error rather than a fetch error), this test may not exercise the intended non-OK response path.

The first test verifies the POST body but does not assert the resulting hook state (e.g., stage transitions to 'idle' or 'complete' after a successful response). Adding a state assertion would make the test more complete.
Good coverage of the non-JSON fallback path — verifying the hook surfaces a status-code-based message when JSON parsing fails is a useful edge case.

+import type { PRAnalysis, ChangeCluster, FileAnalysis, DiffAnnotation } from "../src/types.js";
+
+export function makeDiffAnnotation(overrides: Partial<DiffAnnotation> = {}): DiffAnnotation {
+  return {
+    lineStart: 10,
+    lineEnd: 12,
+    type: "warning",
+    message: "Possible null reference",
+    ...overrides,
+  };
+}
+
+export function makeFileAnalysis(overrides: Partial<FileAnalysis> = {}): FileAnalysis {
+  return {
+    path: "src/utils/helper.ts",
+    summary: "Added helper function",
+    category: "logic",
+    impactScore: 3,
+    diff: `--- a/src/utils/helper.ts\n+++ b/src/utils/helper.ts\n@@ -1,3 +1,5 @@\n import { foo } from "bar";\n+import { baz } from "qux";\n-const old = 1;\n+const new_val = 2;`,
+    annotations: [makeDiffAnnotation()],
+    ...overrides,
+  };
+}
+
+export function makeCluster(overrides: Partial<ChangeCluster> = {}): ChangeCluster {
+  return {
+    id: "cluster-1",
+    name: "Core Logic Changes",
+    summary: "Updates to the main processing pipeline",
+    tag: "needs-review",
+    priority: 1,
+    files: [makeFileAnalysis()],
+    insights: ["Important change to data flow"],
+    ...overrides,
+  };
+}
+
+export function makeAnalysis(overrides: Partial<PRAnalysis> = {}): PRAnalysis {

+    pr: {
+      url: "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/42",
+      title: "Add new feature",
+      author: "testuser",
+      baseBranch: "main",
+      headBranch: "feature/new-thing",
+      additions: 150,
+      deletions: 30,
+      fileCount: 5,

+    executiveSummary: "This PR adds a new feature for processing data.",
+    clusters: [

+      makeCluster({
+        id: "cluster-2",
+        name: "Style Updates",
+        tag: "style-only",
+        priority: 3,
+        summary: "CSS and formatting changes",
+      }),
+    ],
+    timeSaved: "15 minutes",
+    ...overrides,

+}

annotations.message: The inline diff string in makeFileAnalysis uses a raw template literal with escaped newlines which is hard to read; consider extracting it as a named constant or using a dedent helper for clarity.

Factory functions use Partial<T> overrides spread at the end, which is a clean pattern; ensure all required fields remain in sync if the underlying types evolve, as missing fields would only surface at runtime or in consuming tests.

clusters.name: Docker and Compose Configuration
clusters.summary: Multi-stage Dockerfile that builds frontend and backend into a single production image, plus a docker-compose.yml with production and dev profiles (dev profile enables live-reload for both sides). Together these define the entire containerized deployment strategy.

files.summary: Adds a multi-stage Dockerfile that builds the frontend and backend separately before assembling a lean production image. This is significant as it establishes the containerization strategy for the entire application.
files.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+# Stage 1: Build frontend
+FROM node:22-alpine AS frontend-build
+WORKDIR /app/frontend
+COPY frontend/package*.json ./
+RUN npm ci
+COPY frontend/ ./
+RUN npm run build
+
+# Stage 2: Build backend
+FROM node:22-alpine AS backend-build
+WORKDIR /app/backend
+COPY backend/package*.json ./
+RUN npm ci
+COPY backend/ ./
+RUN npm run build
+
+# Stage 3: Production image
+FROM node:22-alpine
+WORKDIR /app
+
+COPY --from=backend-build /app/backend/package*.json ./
+RUN npm ci --omit=dev
+
+COPY --from=backend-build /app/backend/dist ./dist
+COPY --from=frontend-build /app/frontend/dist ./public
+
+ENV NODE_ENV=production
+CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]

annotations.message: The production stage copies package*.json from the backend build stage but runs 'npm ci --omit=dev' without a package-lock.json guarantee from the original source — ensure the lock file is consistently present in the backend build artifact to avoid non-deterministic installs.
Consider pinning the production base image to a specific digest (e.g. node:22-alpine@sha256:...) to prevent unexpected changes from upstream image updates breaking the production environment.
No EXPOSE instruction is present; adding one (e.g. EXPOSE 3000) documents the intended port and makes the image easier to use with orchestration tools like Docker Compose or Kubernetes.
Consider adding a non-root USER directive before the CMD to follow the principle of least privilege in production containers.

files.summary: Adds a new docker-compose.yml with two service definitions: a production app service and a dev service (gated behind a 'dev' profile) with live-reload support for both backend and frontend. This establishes the containerized development and production workflow for the project.
files.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@
+services:
+  app:
+    build: .
+    ports:
+      - "${PORT_PREFIX:-90}00:9000"
+    environment:
+      - PORT=9000
+      - ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}
+      - GITHUB_TOKEN=${GITHUB_TOKEN}
+    env_file:
+      - path: .env
+        required: false
+
+  app-dev:
+    image: node:22-alpine
+    working_dir: /app
+    ports:
+      - "${PORT_PREFIX:-90}00:9000"
+      - "${PORT_PREFIX:-90}01:5173"
+    environment:
+      - PORT=9000
+      - ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}
+      - GITHUB_TOKEN=${GITHUB_TOKEN}
+    env_file:
+      - path: .env
+        required: false
+    volumes:
+      - ./backend:/app/backend
+      - ./frontend:/app/frontend
+      - backend_modules:/app/backend/node_modules
+      - frontend_modules:/app/frontend/node_modules
+    command: >
+      sh -c "
+        cd /app/backend && npm install &&
+        cd /app/frontend && npm install &&
+        cd /app/backend && npx tsx watch src/index.ts &
+        cd /app/frontend && npx vite --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5173
+      "
+    profiles:
+      - dev
+
+volumes:
+  backend_modules:
+  frontend_modules:

annotations.message: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is passed as an environment variable directly from the host shell; if not set in the host environment or .env file, it will be empty and cause runtime failures silently.
GITHUB_TOKEN is passed directly from the host shell; same risk as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — absence is not enforced and may cause hard-to-debug auth failures at runtime.
Both app and app-dev bind to the same host port (${PORT_PREFIX:-90}00:9000), which will cause a conflict if both services are started simultaneously without overriding PORT_PREFIX.

The dev service command runs npm install on every container start, which is slow and fragile in CI or low-bandwidth environments. Consider using a custom Dockerfile or an entrypoint script that only installs when node_modules is missing.
The backend tsx watch process is backgrounded with '&' but there is no error handling; if it crashes, the container will continue running the Vite process with no indication the backend is down.

files.summary: Adds the full design specification for the PR Triage Bot, covering architecture, multi-agent pipeline, data models, API surface, and phased delivery plan. This is the foundational reference document that defines system behavior across all implementation phases.
files.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,240 @@
+# PR Triage Bot — Design Specification
+
+## Overview
+
+A standalone, Dockerized React application that helps developers efficiently triage large pull requests — especially those generated by AI coding agents. The tool uses Claude to analyze PR diffs, group related changes into logical clusters, rank them by importance, and present a layered view that lets reviewers focus on the 10-20% of changes that actually need human attention.
+
+## Target Users
+
+- **MVP:** Individual developers reviewing PRs on GitHub.com (public and private repos). They supply their own Anthropic API key and GitHub token.
+- **Future:** Engineering teams with centralized deployment (GitHub App / CI integration). Architecture should not preclude this path.
+
+## Core Concept: Layered Review
+
+Instead of a flat file diff, the tool presents PR changes at three zoom levels:
+
+1. **Executive Summary** — 2-3 sentences: what the PR does, what needs attention, what's noise.
+2. **Change Clusters** — related changes grouped and ranked by reviewer priority. Each cluster is tagged ("needs-review", "low-risk", "boilerplate", "style-only") with a summary explaining *why* it matters or doesn't.
+3. **Annotated Diffs** — line-by-line diffs within a cluster, with inline agent notes highlighting specific concerns (security issues, logic bugs, convention violations, etc.).
+
+Users navigate via breadcrumbs: `PR Summary → Cluster → File`. Click to drill in, back to zoom out.
+
+## Architecture
+
+### Project Structure
+
+```
+pr-triage-bot/
+├── docker-compose.yml          # Orchestrates all services
+├── Dockerfile                  # Builds frontend + backend together
+├── .env.example                # PORT_PREFIX, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN
+├── .gitignore                  # Includes .env, .superpowers/, node_modules, etc.
+├── frontend/                   # React + TypeScript (Vite)
+│   ├── src/
+│   ├── package.json
+│   └── vite.config.ts
+├── backend/                    # Node.js + TypeScript (Express)
+│   ├── src/
+│   └── package.json
+├── analyzer/                   # Python (FastAPI) — Phase 2+
+│   ├── Dockerfile              # Separate Dockerfile (Python base image)
+│   └── src/
+└── docs/
+```
+
+### Services
+
+**Phase 1 — Single container ("app"):**
+- Express backend serves the Vite-built React frontend as static files
+- In dev mode, Vite dev server runs inside the container with hot reload
+- Backend handles: GitHub API calls, Claude agent orchestration, WebSocket streaming
+
+**Phase 2+ — Adds "analyzer" container:**
+- Python FastAPI sidecar for deep code analysis
+- Backend calls analyzer via internal Docker network HTTP
+- Analyzer handles: repo cloning, AST parsing, dependency graphs, convention checking
+
+### Communication
+
+- **Frontend ↔ Backend:** REST for actions + WebSocket for streaming analysis results
+- **Backend ↔ Analyzer:** Internal HTTP API (Docker network, not exposed externally)
+
+### Worktree-Friendly Dev
+
+- `docker-compose.yml` uses a `PORT_PREFIX` env var (default `90`)
+- Default ports: `9000` (app in dev), `9002` (analyzer)
+- Each git worktree sets a different `PORT_PREFIX` in its `.env` (e.g., `91` → `9100/9102`)
+- Multiple instances can run simultaneously without port conflicts
+- All services have volume mounts for hot reload
+
+## Token / Key Management
+
+Keys are resolved in this order:
+
+1. `.env` file in project root (gitignored) — `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`
+2. Environment variables (for Docker/CI)
+3. Frontend input as fallback — if backend has no keys, UI shows input fields
+
+The frontend checks `GET /api/config/status` on load to determine whether keys are pre-configured. If they are, key input fields are hidden.
+
+Keys sent via the frontend are held in backend memory for the duration of the analysis only — never persisted to disk.
+
+## Multi-Agent Analysis Pipeline
+
+When a user submits a PR URL, the backend orchestrates three Claude agents in sequence:
+
+### Agent 1: File Analyzer
+
+- **Input:** Individual file diffs (chunked to stay within context limits)
+- **Execution:** Runs in parallel across files
+- **Output:** Array of `FileAnalysis` objects
+- **Job:** Summarize each file's changes, categorize (logic/style/config/boilerplate/test), assign initial impact score (1-5)
+
+### Agent 2: Clustering Agent
+
+- **Input:** All `FileAnalysis` results from Agent 1
+- **Output:** Array of `ChangeCluster` objects
+- **Job:** Group related changes into logical clusters, name them descriptively, write cluster-level summaries
+
+### Agent 3: Ranking & Synthesis Agent
+
+- **Input:** All `ChangeCluster` objects from Agent 2
+- **Output:** Final `PRAnalysis` with executive summary
+- **Job:** Rank clusters by reviewer importance, write executive summary, tag clusters (needs-review/low-risk/boilerplate/style-only), generate inline diff annotations for high-priority items
+
+### Streaming UX
+
+Results stream to the frontend via WebSocket as each agent completes:
+
+```
+→ { type: "status", stage: "file-analysis", progress: "12/34 files" }
+→ { type: "status", stage: "clustering", progress: "grouping changes" }
+→ { type: "partial", clusters: [...] }
+→ { type: "status", stage: "ranking" }
+→ { type: "complete", analysis: PRAnalysis }
+```
+
+The user sees the executive summary first, then clusters populate progressively. No waiting for the full pipeline to finish.
+
+## Data Model
+
+```typescript
+interface PRAnalysis {
+  id: string;
+  pr: PRMetadata;
+  executiveSummary: string;
+  clusters: ChangeCluster[];
+  timeSaved: string;
+}
+
+interface PRMetadata {
+  url: string;
+  title: string;
+  author: string;
+  baseBranch: string;
+  headBranch: string;
+  additions: number;
+  deletions: number;
+  fileCount: number;
+}
+
+interface ChangeCluster {
+  id: string;
+  name: string;
+  summary: string;
+  tag: "needs-review" | "low-risk" | "boilerplate" | "style-only";
+  priority: number;
+  files: FileAnalysis[];
+  insights: string[]; // Phase 2+: ripple effects, conventions, etc.
+}
+
+interface FileAnalysis {
+  path: string;
+  summary: string;
+  category: "logic" | "style" | "config" | "test" | "boilerplate" | "docs";
+  impactScore: number;
+  diff: string;
+  annotations: DiffAnnotation[];
+}
+
+interface DiffAnnotation {
+  lineStart: number;
+  lineEnd: number;
+  type: "warning" | "info" | "suggestion";
+  message: string;
+}
+```
+
+## API Surface
+
+```
+# Phase 1
+POST /api/analyze              — start analysis (PR URL, optional keys)
+GET  /api/analysis/:id         — get analysis result
+GET  /api/config/status        — check if API keys are configured
+WS   /ws                       — stream analysis progress & results
+
+# Phase 2+
+POST /api/analyze/deep         — trigger deep analysis with repo clone
+GET  /api/analysis/:id/graph   — get dependency graph data
+```
+
+## Phase Breakdown
+
+### Phase 1: Core MVP (Frontend + Backend + Agent Pipeline)
+
+- Landing page: PR URL input, optional API key inputs (hidden if .env configured)
+- GitHub API integration: fetch PR metadata, file list, diffs
+- Multi-agent pipeline: File Analyzer → Clustering Agent → Ranking Agent
+- Layered UI: executive summary → change clusters → annotated diffs
+- WebSocket streaming for progressive result display
+- Dockerized: single `docker compose up`, parameterized ports
+- Hot reload in dev mode
+
+**Delivers:** A working tool that takes a PR URL and gives you a prioritized, clustered review with inline annotations.
+
+### Phase 2: Deep Code Analysis (Python Analyzer Sidecar)
+
+- Shallow clone of the repo into the analyzer container
+- AST parsing via tree-sitter for multi-language support
+- Dependency graph construction: what functions/modules does this change touch, what depends on them
+- "Ripple effect" analysis: identify callers/dependents that may be affected by changes
+- Convention checking: does new code follow existing naming, structure, error handling patterns
+- Redundancy detection: did the PR introduce functionality that already exists
+- Test coverage assessment: are changed code paths covered by tests
+- Results enrich each `ChangeCluster` and `FileAnalysis` with structural insights
+
+**Delivers:** Analysis that goes beyond LLM inference — grounded in actual code structure.
+
+### Phase 3: Semantic Understanding (Knowledge Graph)
+
+- In-memory knowledge graph (NetworkX) built from repo code structure
+- Maps relationships: calls, imports, inherits, implements, tests
+- Cross-file impact scoring: changes to highly-connected nodes scored as higher risk
+- Enhanced agent prompts include graph context for smarter clustering and ranking
+- Optional graph visualization showing change impact radius
+- Swappable storage backend (can upgrade to embedded DB or Neo4j later)
+
+**Delivers:** Holistic codebase understanding — the analysis knows not just what changed, but how it connects to everything else.
+
+## Tech Stack Summary
+
+| Component | Technology | Phase |
+|-----------|-----------|-------|
+| Frontend | React + TypeScript + Vite | 1 |
+| Backend | Node.js + Express + TypeScript | 1 |
+| AI | Claude API (Anthropic TypeScript SDK) | 1 |
+| GitHub Integration | GitHub REST/GraphQL API (Octokit) | 1 |
+| Real-time | WebSocket (ws library) | 1 |
+| Containerization | Docker + Docker Compose | 1 |
+| Code Analysis | Python + FastAPI + tree-sitter | 2 |
+| Knowledge Graph | Python + NetworkX | 3 |
+
+## Non-Goals (for now)
+
+- GitHub Enterprise Server or GitLab/Bitbucket support
+- Persistent storage / database (analyses are ephemeral)
+- User accounts or multi-tenancy
+- GitHub App / webhook integration
+- Commenting directly on PRs from the tool
+- Support for non-GitHub PR URLs

annotations.message: Key resolution order is well-defined, but the fallback to frontend-supplied keys held only in memory should be clearly communicated to users in the UI to avoid confusion about security posture.

The pipeline is described as strictly sequential (Agent 1 → Agent 2 → Agent 3), but Agent 1 runs in parallel across files. Consider explicitly noting failure/partial-failure semantics — what happens if some file analyses fail before clustering begins?
The streaming WebSocket protocol is clearly specified; ensure the backend implementation handles back-pressure or slow consumers so a stalled WebSocket connection doesn't block the agent pipeline.

GET /api/analysis/:id has no mention of authentication or ownership checks. In a multi-user or team deployment (Phase 2+), any user who guesses an analysis ID could retrieve another user's PR data, including diffs from private repos.

Phase 1 lists 'hot reload in dev mode' as a deliverable but the architecture section notes Vite dev server runs inside the container — document how volume mounts are wired so contributors don't hit stale-cache issues when iterating on frontend code.

files.summary: Adds a comprehensive 17-task implementation plan for the Phase 1 MVP of the PR Triage Bot, covering full-stack scaffolding, three Claude agent pipeline, WebSocket streaming, REST API, React frontend, and Docker deployment. This plan serves as the authoritative blueprint for the entire initial build.

annotations.message: Plan mandates use of superpowers:subagent-driven-development or superpowers:executing-plans skills for agentic workers — good guardrail for consistent execution.
Backend package.json pins @anthropic-ai/sdk at ^0.39.0 and express at ^5.1.0 — both are relatively recent major versions; confirm compatibility before locking in the project.

The file-analyzer prompt instructs Claude to respond with JSON only but does not include a system prompt enforcing JSON mode; consider adding a system message or using structured output to reduce parse failures.
analyzeFile parses Claude's response with JSON.parse without try/catch; a malformed response will crash the pipeline mid-run with an unhandled rejection rather than a recoverable error.
clusterFiles also calls JSON.parse without error handling; same crash risk as file-analyzer — both agents should wrap parsing in try/catch and emit a structured error event.
In-memory analyses Map will be lost on server restart; this is noted as intentional for the MVP but should be flagged for Phase 2 persistence.
Pipeline error handler sets status back to 'running' instead of an error state — GET /api/analysis/:id will return stale 'running' indefinitely if the pipeline fails, leaving clients polling forever.

index.ts mounts analyzeRouter twice (app.use('/api/analyze') and app.get('/api/analysis/:id', analyzeRouter)) — the second mount is incorrect; the GET /:id route is already defined inside the router and will be served at /api/analyze/:id, not /api/analysis/:id.

This matters because it provides a structured roadmap for addressing critical code review findings and achieving 80%+ test coverage.

@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+# Phase 1 Code Review Fixes & Test Coverage Plan
+
+**Goal:** Fix all critical/important issues from code review, then achieve 80%+ test coverage.
+
+---
+
+## Fix 1: JSON Parse Safety in All Agents
+- Add `extractJSON` helper that strips markdown fences and handles parse errors
+- Add try/catch with descriptive errors in all 3 agents
+- Validate response has text content before parsing
+
+## Fix 2: Pipeline Error Handling
+- Update `startPipeline` catch block to call `setAnalysis(id, { status: "error", error })` 
+- Add try/catch inside `runPipeline` that sends error WSMessage
+- Handle zero-files edge case
+
+## Fix 3: Ranking Agent Non-null Safety
+- Guard `clusterMap.get(update.id)` — skip unknown IDs instead of crashing
+- Validate all input files appear in at least one cluster after clustering
+
+## Fix 4: Frontend Error Handling
+- Wrap `JSON.parse` in useWebSocket with try/catch
+- Wrap entire `startAnalysis` in try/catch for network errors
+- Guard `res.json()` call for non-JSON error responses
+
+## Fix 5: SPA Wildcard Route Fix
+- Exclude `/api/*` paths from the catch-all
+- Return proper 404 for unknown API routes
+
+## Fix 6: Analysis Store TTL
+- Add max size + TTL eviction to analyses map
+
+## Fix 7: GitHub Pagination
+- Paginate `listFiles` to handle PRs with >100 files
+- Filter out binary files (no patch)
+
+## Fix 8: Concurrency Limit
+- Add p-limit for parallel Claude API calls in pipeline
+
+## Fix 9: Frontend Accessibility & UX Fixes
+- ClusterList: add keyboard support (role, tabIndex, onKeyDown)
+- Breadcrumbs: use buttons instead of `<a href="#">`, add aria-label
+- DiffView: exclude `---`/`+++`/`@@` lines from coloring
+- Remove dead `analysisId` state from App.tsx
+- Remove unused `onAnalysisStarted` prop
+
+## Fix 10: Comprehensive Unit Tests
+- Backend: error cases, edge cases, all untested paths
+- Frontend: all components, hooks, error states
+- Target: 80%+ coverage

annotations.message: Fix 1 targets JSON parse safety across all agents — worth ensuring the extractJSON helper is tested for edge cases like nested fences and malformed partial JSON.
Fix 2 should clarify whether the error WSMessage is sent before or after calling setAnalysis so the frontend doesn't enter a race between status updates.
Fix 3 only skips unknown cluster IDs silently; consider logging a warning so silent data loss is detectable during debugging.
Fix 7 mentions filtering binary files with no patch, but the plan should also specify behavior when all files in a PR are binary to avoid an empty-pipeline edge case.
Fix 8 introduces p-limit for concurrency but does not specify the concurrency ceiling; the plan should document the chosen limit and the rationale (e.g., API rate limits).

@@ -0,0 +1,2212 @@
+# PR Triage Bot — Phase 2: Deep Code Analysis Implementation Plan
+
+> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
+
+**Goal:** Add a Python FastAPI sidecar container that performs structural code analysis — AST parsing, dependency graphs, convention checking, redundancy detection, and test coverage assessment — enriching the Phase 1 LLM-only analysis with grounded, code-structure-based insights.
+
+**Architecture:** New `analyzer` service (Python + FastAPI) runs alongside the existing Node.js backend in Docker Compose. Backend calls analyzer via internal Docker network HTTP. Analyzer shallow-clones the repo, parses it with tree-sitter, builds dependency graphs, and returns structural insights that enrich `ChangeCluster.insights` and `FileAnalysis.annotations`. A new `POST /api/analyze/deep` endpoint triggers the enhanced pipeline.
+
+**Tech Stack:** Python 3.12, FastAPI, uvicorn, tree-sitter + language grammars (Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Rust, Java), gitpython (for shallow clone), pytest.
+
+**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-02-pr-triage-bot-design.md` — Phase 2 section.
+
+**Prerequisite:** Phase 1 MVP must be complete and working.
+
+---
+
+## File Structure
+
+```
+analyzer/
+├── Dockerfile                      # Python 3.12-slim, installs tree-sitter grammars
+├── pyproject.toml                  # Project config, dependencies, pytest config
+├── src/
+│   ├── main.py                     # FastAPI app entry point
+│   ├── models.py                   # Pydantic models matching backend types
+│   ├── routers/
+│   │   └── analyze.py              # POST /analyze — main analysis endpoint
+│   ├── services/
+│   │   ├── repo.py                 # Shallow clone + cleanup
+│   │   ├── parser.py               # tree-sitter parsing: extract functions, classes, imports
+│   │   ├── dependency_graph.py     # Build caller/callee graph from parsed symbols
+│   │   ├── ripple_effect.py        # Find affected dependents of changed symbols
+│   │   ├── conventions.py          # Check naming, structure, error handling patterns
+│   │   ├── redundancy.py           # Detect if new code duplicates existing functionality
+│   │   └── test_coverage.py        # Assess whether changed code paths have test coverage
+│   └── utils/
+│       └── tree_sitter_langs.py    # Language detection + grammar loading
+├── tests/
+│   ├── conftest.py                 # Shared fixtures (sample repos, parsed trees)
+│   ├── test_parser.py
+│   ├── test_dependency_graph.py
+│   ├── test_ripple_effect.py
+│   ├── test_conventions.py
+│   ├── test_redundancy.py
+│   ├── test_test_coverage.py
+│   └── test_api.py                 # Integration test for the FastAPI endpoint
+│
+backend/  (modifications to existing Phase 1 code)
+├── src/
+│   ├── services/
+│   │   └── analyzer-client.ts      # HTTP client to call the analyzer sidecar
+│   ├── routes/
+│   │   └── analyze.ts              # Add POST /api/analyze/deep
+│   └── services/
+│       └── pipeline.ts             # Extend pipeline to merge structural insights
+├── tests/
+│   └── services/
+│       └── analyzer-client.test.ts
+│
+docker-compose.yml                  # Add analyzer service
+```
+
+---
+
+## Task 1: Analyzer Project Scaffolding
+
+**Files:**
+- Create: `analyzer/pyproject.toml`
+- Create: `analyzer/src/main.py`
+- Create: `analyzer/src/models.py`
+- Create: `analyzer/Dockerfile`
+
+- [ ] **Step 1: Create analyzer/pyproject.toml**
+
+```toml
+[project]
+name = "pr-triage-analyzer"
+version = "0.1.0"
+requires-python = ">=3.12"
+dependencies = [
+    "fastapi>=0.115.0",
+    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.34.0",
+    "tree-sitter>=0.24.0",
+    "tree-sitter-python>=0.23.0",
+    "tree-sitter-javascript>=0.23.0",
+    "tree-sitter-typescript>=0.23.0",
+    "tree-sitter-go>=0.23.0",
+    "tree-sitter-rust>=0.23.0",
+    "tree-sitter-java>=0.23.0",
+    "gitpython>=3.1.0",
+    "pydantic>=2.10.0",
+]
+
+[project.optional-dependencies]
+dev = [
+    "pytest>=8.3.0",
+    "pytest-asyncio>=0.25.0",
+    "httpx>=0.28.0",
+]
+
+[tool.pytest.ini_options]
+testpaths = ["tests"]
+asyncio_mode = "auto"
+```
+
+- [ ] **Step 2: Create analyzer/src/models.py**
+
+Pydantic models that mirror the backend TypeScript types, plus analyzer-specific types:
+
+```python
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+
+class AnalyzeRequest(BaseModel):
+    repo_url: str
+    base_branch: str
+    head_branch: str
+    changed_files: list[str]
+
+
+class SymbolInfo(BaseModel):
+    name: str
+    kind: str  # "function", "class", "method", "variable"
+    file_path: str
+    line_start: int
+    line_end: int
+
+
+class DependencyEdge(BaseModel):
+    source: str  # "file:symbol"
+    target: str  # "file:symbol"
+    kind: str  # "calls", "imports", "inherits"
+
+
+class RippleEffect(BaseModel):
+    changed_symbol: str
+    affected_symbols: list[str]
+    risk_level: str  # "high", "medium", "low"
+    reason: str
+
+
+class ConventionViolation(BaseModel):
+    file_path: str
+    line: int
+    rule: str
+    message: str
+    severity: str  # "warning", "info"
+
+
+class RedundancyMatch(BaseModel):
+    new_code_file: str
+    new_code_symbol: str
+    existing_file: str
+    existing_symbol: str
+    similarity: float
+    message: str
+
+
+class TestCoverageGap(BaseModel):
+    file_path: str
+    symbol: str
+    has_test: bool
+    test_file: str | None
+    message: str
+
+
+class FileInsights(BaseModel):
+    file_path: str
+    ripple_effects: list[RippleEffect]
+    convention_violations: list[ConventionViolation]
+    redundancies: list[RedundancyMatch]
+    test_coverage_gaps: list[TestCoverageGap]

+from tree_sitter import Node
+from src.models import SymbolInfo
+from src.utils.tree_sitter_langs import detect_language, get_parser
+
+# tree-sitter node types that represent symbols we care about, per language
+SYMBOL_QUERIES: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {
+    "python": {
+        "function_definition": "function",
+        "class_definition": "class",
+    },
+    "typescript": {
+        "function_declaration": "function",
+        "class_declaration": "class",
+        "method_definition": "method",
+    },
+    "javascript": {
+        "function_declaration": "function",
+        "class_declaration": "class",
+        "method_definition": "method",
+    },
+    "go": {
+        "function_declaration": "function",
+        "method_declaration": "method",
+        "type_declaration": "class",
+    },
+    "rust": {
+        "function_item": "function",
+        "impl_item": "class",
+        "struct_item": "class",
+    },
+    "java": {
+        "method_declaration": "method",
+        "class_declaration": "class",
+    },
+}
+
+
+def _get_name(node: Node) -> str | None:
+    for child in node.children:
+        if child.type in ("identifier", "name", "type_identifier", "property_identifier"):
+            return child.text.decode("utf-8") if child.text else None
+    return None
+
+
+def _walk_tree(
+    node: Node,
+    file_path: str,
+    language: str,
+    parent_kind: str | None = None,
+) -> list[SymbolInfo]:
+    symbols: list[SymbolInfo] = []
+    node_types = SYMBOL_QUERIES.get(language, {})
+
+    if node.type in node_types:
+        name = _get_name(node)
+        if name:
+            kind = node_types[node.type]
+            # Python methods are functions inside a class
+            if language == "python" and kind == "function" and parent_kind == "class":
+                kind = "method"
+            symbols.append(
+                SymbolInfo(
+                    name=name,
+                    kind=kind,
+                    file_path=file_path,
+                    line_start=node.start_point[0] + 1,
+                    line_end=node.end_point[0] + 1,
+                )
+            )
+
+    for child in node.children:
+        child_parent = node_types.get(node.type, parent_kind)
+        symbols.extend(_walk_tree(child, file_path, language, child_parent))
+
+    return symbols
+
+
+def extract_symbols(file_path: str) -> list[SymbolInfo]:
+    language = detect_language(file_path)
+    if language is None:
+        return []
+
+    parser = get_parser(language)
+    if parser is None:
+        return []
+
+    with open(file_path, "rb") as f:
+        source = f.read()
+
+    tree = parser.parse(source)
+    return _walk_tree(tree.root_node, file_path, language)
+```

+from src.utils.tree_sitter_langs import detect_language, get_parser
+
+# Import node types per language
+IMPORT_NODE_TYPES: dict[str, list[str]] = {
+    "python": ["import_statement", "import_from_statement"],
+    "typescript": ["import_statement"],
+    "javascript": ["import_statement"],
+    "go": ["import_declaration"],
+    "rust": ["use_declaration"],
+    "java": ["import_declaration"],
+}
+
+
+def _extract_import_source(node: Node, language: str) -> str | None:
+    if language == "python":
+        for child in node.children:
+            if child.type == "dotted_name":
+                return child.text.decode("utf-8") if child.text else None
+        # import_from_statement: look for module_name
+        for child in node.children:
+            if child.type == "module_name" or (
+                child.type == "dotted_name" and node.type == "import_from_statement"
+            ):
+                return child.text.decode("utf-8") if child.text else None
+
+    if language in ("typescript", "javascript"):
+        for child in node.children:
+            if child.type == "string":
+                text = child.text.decode("utf-8") if child.text else ""
+                return text.strip("\"'")
+
+    return node.text.decode("utf-8") if node.text else None
+
+
+def _find_imports(root: Node, language: str) -> list[str]:
+    import_types = IMPORT_NODE_TYPES.get(language, [])
+    sources: list[str] = []
+
+    def walk(node: Node) -> None:
+        if node.type in import_types:
+            source = _extract_import_source(node, language)
+            if source:
+                sources.append(source)
+        for child in node.children:
+            walk(child)
+
+    walk(root)
+    return sources
+
+
+def build_dependency_graph(
+    repo_dir: str,
+    changed_files: list[str],
+) -> list[DependencyEdge]:
+    edges: list[DependencyEdge] = []
+
+    for file_path in changed_files:
+        full_path = os.path.join(repo_dir, file_path)
+        if not os.path.isfile(full_path):
+            continue
+
+        language = detect_language(file_path)
+        if language is None:
+            continue
+
+        parser = get_parser(language)
+        if parser is None:
+            continue
+
+        with open(full_path, "rb") as f:
+            source = f.read()
+
+        tree = parser.parse(source)
+        imports = _find_imports(tree.root_node, language)
+
+        for imp in imports:
+            edges.append(
+                DependencyEdge(
+                    source=file_path,
+                    target=imp,
+                    kind="imports",
+                )
+            )
+
+    return edges

+        # Normalize target: "utils" matches "utils.py"
+        target = edge.target
+        reverse[target].append(edge.source)
+        # Also register with .py stripped for matching
+        if target.endswith(".py"):
+            reverse[target[:-3]].append(edge.source)
+    return reverse
+
+
+def _file_stem(file_path: str) -> str:
+    """Get file stem without extension: 'utils.py' -> 'utils'."""
+    if "." in file_path:
+        return file_path.rsplit(".", 1)[0]
+    return file_path
+
+
+def find_ripple_effects(
+    symbols: list[SymbolInfo],
+    edges: list[DependencyEdge],
+    changed_files: list[str],
+    max_depth: int = 3,
+) -> list[RippleEffect]:
+    reverse_graph = _build_reverse_graph(edges)
+    results: list[RippleEffect] = []
+
+    for changed_file in changed_files:
+        # Find all files that transitively depend on this changed file
+        affected: list[str] = []
+        visited: set[str] = set()
+        queue: list[tuple[str, int]] = [(changed_file, 0)]
+
+        # Also try matching by stem
+        stem = _file_stem(changed_file)
+
+        while queue:
+            current, depth = queue.pop(0)
+            if depth >= max_depth:
+                continue
+
+            current_stem = _file_stem(current)
+            dependents: list[str] = []
+            dependents.extend(reverse_graph.get(current, []))
+            dependents.extend(reverse_graph.get(current_stem, []))
+
+            for dep in dependents:
+                if dep not in visited and dep != changed_file:
+                    visited.add(dep)
+                    affected.append(dep)
+                    queue.append((dep, depth + 1))
+
+        if affected:
+            risk = "high" if len(affected) >= 3 else "medium" if len(affected) >= 1 else "low"
+            results.append(
+                RippleEffect(
+                    changed_symbol=changed_file,
+                    affected_symbols=affected,
+                    risk_level=risk,
+                    reason=f"Changes to {changed_file} may affect {len(affected)} dependent file(s)",
+                )
+            )
+
+    return results
+```

+                    rule=f"{symbol.kind}-naming",
+                    message=f"{symbol.kind.capitalize()} '{symbol.name}' doesn't follow {language} convention ({expected_style})",
+                    severity="info",
+                )
